p: It is brought in the Tikkunim
"When she receives from the Supernal Mother,
כְּמָה דְּאַתְּ אָמַר (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים ג, יא)
"with the crown with which his mother crowned him
on the day of his wedding and on the day of the joy of his heart";
"on the day of his wedding" — this is the lower Shechinah;
"and on the day of the joy of his heart" —
For the matter of the lower Shechinah
is fear, from the aspect of the lower Hei;
as is brought from the Rambam, of blessed memory
(cited in the Rema at the beginning of Orach Chaim),
that the Jewish soul is predisposed to this:
that as soon as he considers
that Hashem is standing before him,
at once fear and dread fall upon him.
And this is the aspect of the Name Adnus,
"And if I am a master, where is My fear?"
And this is "on the day of his wedding" —
for at Matan Torah there was
אוּלָם יֵשׁ עִנְיָן עוֹד יוֹתֵר פְּנִימִי,
However, there is a still more inward matter,
"And they shall enter the caves of the rocks
from before the dread of Hashem and from the splendor of His majesty";
this is the revelation of the Shechinah (Pesach Haggadah);
and this is the aspect of the upper Shechinah,
which is called "the day of the joy of his heart";
into the inwardness of the heart,
and from this the heart is filled with joy;
and this is the aspect of Simchas Torah.
And although the lower fear, too,
through the stirring of one's heart —
כִּי בְּלֹא זֶה נֶאֱמַר (מִשְׁלֵי יז, טז)
for without this it is said (Mishlei 17:16),
"Why is there a price in the hand of a fool
to acquire wisdom, when he has no heart?" —
only the aspect of the revealed heart;
that is, only in "the heart of the wise man at his right,"
but "the heart of the fool at his left"
is still in its full force.
But the aspect of the upper Shechinah,
called "the day of the joy of his heart,"
means that the entire inwardness of his heart
becomes full of words of Torah,
until even the heart of the fool
And as is brought in the Tikkunim
"Binah is the heart, and with it the heart understands."
וְיֵשׁ רֶמֶז לָזֶה בַּפָּסוּק (מִשְׁלֵי יח, ב)
And there is an allusion to this in the pasuk (Mishlei 18:2),
but only that his heart be revealed."
that words of Torah should enter it
in the inwardness of the heart —
that through this it will be purged
"But only that his heart be revealed":
that is, to this at least
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה לֹא יִתְבָּעֵר
because through this it will not be purged,
עַל כָּל פָּנִים, מִלֵּב כְּסִיל לִשְׂמֹאלוֹ.
at any rate, from the fool's heart at his left.
